extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting to arXiv (arXiv submitters)
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and criteria used by arXiv moderators to evaluate, classify, decline, reclassify, or remove submissions before and after public announcement. Aimed at guiding authors on acceptable content, formats, and expectations for posting to arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: General expectation for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Material submitted to arXiv is expected to be self-contained and of interest, relevance, and value to the disciplines we serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv moderation is not peer review; arXiv staff and moderators cannot give feedback on the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation occurs before public announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The moderation process primarily occurs after a user submits a work and before the work is made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each work is evaluated based on its content. arXiv moderation decisions may be influenced by the publication status of the submission, but prior publication does not guarantee acceptance. Submitters with previously delayed or declined works should anticipate closer scrutiny; in some cases authors may be required to establish a conventional publication record and limit submissions to works published in conventional journals. arXiv reserves the right to reclassify or decline any submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclassification of works
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators ensure submissions are posted to the most relevant category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-lists may be added to other related categories, or removed when classification is deemed inappropriate. A submission cross-listed to a category will be announced in that category's mailings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline discretion (examples and reservation of right)
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv may decline to post works in its sole discretion; provided list of example topics could lead to decline (not exhaustive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some works published or accepted by a journal may still be declined at arXiv’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly standards (form and language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must comply with appropriate standards of scholarly communication in form, including appropriate and carefully prepared sections, figures, tables, references, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language standards require professional communication and a sufficiently neutral tone (see Code of Conduct). General scrupulousness and care of preparation are required; submissions in need of significant review and revision may be declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly interest (originality, significance, integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be of scholarly archival interest to the communities they represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A submission may be declined if moderators determine it lacks originality, novelty, significance, and/or contains falsified, plagiarized content or serious misrepresentations of data, affiliation, or content. Submissions should focus entirely on the scientific research and avoid extraneous personal or political statements. Items that do not contain original or substantive research — including course projects, research proposals, news, or information about political causes — may be declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types (research articles primary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research articles are the primary content-type submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For submissions other than research articles see the specific content type policies (i.e., other content types have distinct requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For information about submission format requirements please see specific format requirements (the policy points authors to detailed format guidance elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Images (sensitivity and potential for decline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be aware that the use of some images may cause offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include obscenity; sexualized images; images of violence or its results; images with complicated provenance (e.g., the 'Lena' image); politically controversial images; covertly sexual images. The use of essentially any image can be justified by appropriate circumstances, but authors should think carefully. Papers identified as using images likely to cause egregious offense may be declined or removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for authors' use of generative AI language tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must report significant use of sophisticated tools, including text-to-text generative AI, consistent with subject standards for methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors take full responsibility for all contents irrespective of how contents were generated. If generative AI generates inappropriate language, plagiarized content, biased content, errors, incorrect references, or misleading content included in works, the author(s) are responsible. Generative AI language tools should not be listed as an author; instead authors should refer to their use as they would other instruments/software.

rubrics_metrics.name: On topics not covered or communities not served
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv may decline submissions that do not fit into the current classification scheme or where arXiv does not currently serve the intended audience community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While arXiv serves a variety of scientific communities, not all subjects are currently covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicated content / multiple similar submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors make multiple similar submissions or a new submission appears to be a revision of a recent submission, moderators may request consolidation or versioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may ask that submissions be consolidated or indicated as new versions rather than separate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights to submit material / copyright & license authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be the author’s original work, and submitters must have legal authority to grant the selected license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure the submission does not, to the best of their knowledge, infringe anyone's copyright. arXiv does not accept work containing verbatim referee comments, plagiarized content, or works barred by third-party copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive submission rate
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a practical limit to the rate at which appropriate independent submissions can be produced by any one person; arXiv may request an author limit their submission rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author has a backlog of work, arXiv asks that they submit no more than three papers per day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-announcement moderation (withdrawal, removal, reclassification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once announced a paper becomes part of the permanent scholarly record; arXiv will consider removal only if the submitter did not have legal right to agree to the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases where public papers are found to violate arXiv policy, arXiv may withdraw the paper, indicate the concern in the Comments metadata, decline or remove content, or reclassify announced papers if moderators determine a more appropriate category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to appeal classification of an announced article or the decision to decline a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals require carefully reading the appeals process to ensure the request is fully considered. Some cases may require acceptance for publication in a conventional journal before an appeal is considered. Decisions upon appeal are final, and no feedback will be provided with the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who arXiv moderators are and limits on contact
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv moderators are volunteer subject matter experts with terminal degrees who evaluate submissions and categories following arXiv policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators are approved by discipline-level advisory committees and by arXiv staff. Moderation is a professional responsibility; moderators consider submissions as privileged information and respect confidentiality. It is inappropriate to contact moderators directly about submissions; all communication must go through the user support portal or moderation@arxiv.org. Unusual cases may be addressed to the Section Chair via the support portal, but Section Chairs will seldom override a moderator on content judgment and will review procedural issues.
